names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Σολόχων, Παμφαμήρ και Παμφυλών», with the rank word left off; the life page carries «Αγιος Παμφαμηρ» as its own head name.

Read out of the body of the Охридски пролог's second entry for 17. мај ст. ст., „То исто учинише и два његова друга: Памфамир и Памфалон“, where the name stands in the nominative; свети, which the next sentence puts before it, is not a rank. **The spelling is this book's own**, Памфамир against the Greek «Παμφαμήρ» this folder also carries, and a copied script form is stored as printed and never corrected towards another language's. Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: no folder in the corpus holds this form in any language.

The nominative the day page's own `/name/` link carries in its `title`, «Памфамир Халкидонский» — alone of the day's three it carries no rank abbreviation at all — with the place epithet kept. The day's own line declines the three together, «Мчч. Солохона , Памфамира и Памфалона воинов (284-305).» `fk.mjs` on «Памфамир Халкидонский» returned NONE before the write.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 17 мая ст. ст. — «Мчч. Солохона , Памфамира и Памфалона воинов (284-305).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day and the same three soldiers; this folder already carries the other two as `related` rows. **`dates` were not touched: the folder has none and the Russian gives no year of its own**, only the reign «в царствование императора Максимиана (284–305)», which the day line prints as a span. A reign is not a death year, and the 298 the Serbian book gives the leader of the three was not copied across to him. The one thing the Russian adds about him in particular is that he and the third of them died under the first torture, before their leader's long ordeal began. His `/name/` link's title is the only one of the three that carries no rank abbreviation. The day page prints no hymn for the three. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Σολόχων, Παμφαμήρ και Παμφυλών»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives him as one of three head names on one page — hence three folders. **He is not one of the corpus's Pamphili**, which the namesweep raised: Pamphamer is a different name, and `pamphilus-of-caesarea`, `pamphilus-the-martyr` and the companions named after that man are other people on other days. **No year, so no `dates` object**, and no `locations` although Egypt and Chalcedon are named. **The page's second couplet is his and Pamphylon's together** — take courage even though you are beaten, you two martyrs; God will make of your wounds a soothing balm, and crowns — and he is named in it only as one of the two.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.05.2026 (17. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Солохон.“ — „То исто учинише и два његова друга: Памфамир и Памфалон … под којима издахнуше свети Памфамир и Памфалон.“

attestations.note: **A ROW OWED OUT OF A COMPANION'S HEADING.** The Prologue heads the entry „Свети мученик Солохон.“ and names him in the body twice: as one of the two comrades who declared themselves Christians when Solochon did, and as one of the two who **expired under the tortures**. **A martyrdom narrated is the test that owes a row**, as `laodicius-the-jailer`'s was on 13 May and as Junia's is on this same day; so the `text` quotes the heading whole and then his own two clauses. He is on the same menologion 17/5 the Greek row already carries. **A YEAR READ AND DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN.** „предста Господу … 298. године“ is given for **Solochon**, in the sentence that follows his revival in the widow's house; Pamphamer and Pamphylon died earlier in the same torture and **the Prologue gives them no year of their own**. Taking Solochon's 298 for them would be inferring a year the page does not state of them, which BRIEF.md §4 forbids, so **`dates` is untouched and this folder stays `undated`** while his companion's now carries 298. **That asymmetry is deliberate and it is the author's to close in one commit if the reading is wanted** — the three died in one episode and no calendar read for the corpus dates the two. **New here**: that **they declared themselves Christians when the imperial order came that all soldiers sacrifice**, which is the Prologue's own framing of the refusal, and that the officer was „војвода“, a commander, rather than the tribune of the Greek page. `types` untouched — мученик is the `martyr` and the soldiering is in the entry's first sentence about Solochon. No `locations`; the Prologue names no place, where saint.gr has Chalcedon. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
